samples.summary: A transient share-link fetch failure now tears down the whole live editor session
samples.evidence: `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: 60_000`, `retry: 1` and the render guard `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. In react-query v5 a *background refetch* failure sets `error` while `data` (the previously resolved link) is still present, so this guard fires on a query that still holds a perfectly good `resolved`. Two consecutive failed attempts ~1s apart — one offline blip, a 502, a laptop wake — unmount `SharedDocumentInner` and with it the Yorkie DocumentProvider/editor, replacing a working session with "Link unavailable" and discarding any local Yorkie changes not yet pushed. The comment claims only a "sustained failure" evicts, but nothing in the code distinguishes sustained from momentary (no `errorUpdateCount` threshold, no `resolved &&` fallback). The pre-change code could not evict at all once resolved.

samples.summary: Undo floor now depends on reference identity of an SDK test-accessor's return value
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` was rewritten from a depth comparison to `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1`, where `stack` comes from `this.doc.getUndoStackForTest()`. This is only correct if that accessor returns the *live* internal array whose element identities are stable across calls. If the SDK returns a fresh/copied array of entries (or ever rebuilds an entry, e.g. during change transformation on remote merge), `lastIndexOf` yields -1 and `canUndo()` becomes unconditionally true — the initial-load floor disappears and a user can undo past `setDocument`, which the surrounding comment says 'would destroy blocks the cursor still references'. I could not verify the SDK behaviour: `node_modules` is not present in this checkout and only `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:58` describes the accessor ('arrays of reverse-op batches'). Worth confirming against @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.8 before relying on identity.

samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the notes effect deps rebuilds the store, but YorkieNoteStore's constructor subscription is never released
samples.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor calls `doc.subscribe(...)` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143) and the class exposes no `dispose()`; the effect cleanup at notes-view.tsx:150-155 only calls `editor.dispose()` and nulls `storeRef`. Before this change the effect ran once per document, so the subscription lived as long as the doc. Now a `/shared/:token` role flip (the scenario the change exists for) re-runs the effect and each rebuild leaves another orphaned store subscribed to a document that outlives it — exactly the leak `docs-view.tsx` fixed in this same diff with the new `store.dispose()` (docs-view.tsx:574). The stale callbacks only mutate dead objects, so the cost is the leak plus wasted work rather than wrong output.

samples.summary: One-shot `new YorkieDocStore(doc).setDocument(...)` is never disposed, leaking the constructor subscription
samples.evidence: `new YorkieDocStore(doc).setDocument(content.document)` creates a store whose constructor now registers `this.unsubscribeDoc = doc.subscribe(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:631). The temporary is dropped immediately but the subscription keeps it alive for the document's whole lifetime, marking a dead store dirty on every remote change. The diff adds exactly the `dispose()` this call site needs; it is the one remaining construction site that does not call it.

samples.summary: `catch {}` around the Cmd+Shift+V write silently swallows store/write failures, not just clipboard errors
samples.evidence: The `try` block at 4244-4268 now contains `saveSnapshot()` and the whole `withUndoUnit(...)` write body. `Doc.batch` rethrows after refreshing, and `YorkieDocStore.batch` rolls the update back — but the bare `catch { /* Clipboard API unavailable or permission denied */ }` absorbs that too, so a failed paste (e.g. `Block not found` from a concurrently deleted caret block) leaves an undo checkpoint pushed by `saveSnapshot()`, no content, and no diagnostic. The comment documents only the clipboard failure mode. (Pre-existing shape, but the try now covers a batch that can throw for store reasons.)

samples.summary: `requestLayoutRefresh` leaves `dirtyBlockIds` as an empty Set where a real render left `undefined`, weakening the full-recompute safety net inside an undo unit
samples.evidence: `recomputeLayout()` always ends with `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (editor.ts:1534), which makes the *next* `computeLayout` ignore the cache entirely (`canUseCache` requires `dirtyBlockIds != null`, layout.ts:456). The new seam restores `dirty ?? new Set()`, so after an intra-unit refresh the deferred paint consults the cache for every block. Any write later in the same unit that calls neither `markDirty()` nor `invalidateLayout()` — previously still repainted correctly because the set was `undefined` — will now be silently missed and the committed paint will show stale layout. I walked the composite units (`handleInput`, `applyPastePlan`/`insertBlocks`/`insertPlainText`/`pasteTableCells`, `handleEnter`, `handlePageBreak`, `insertText`, the Hangul path) and each does mark or invalidate, so I found no live instance — but the invariant that used to make an omission harmless is gone, and `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` in `applyPastePlan` is already an unmarked whole-document write riding on it.
searchedFor: grep markDirty/invalidateLayout inside every withUndoUnit body

samples.summary: The deferred render replay runs inside `finally` and can mask the original exception
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s `finally` calls `this.requestRender()` (→ the host's real layout+paint) while an exception from `this.doc.batch(fn)` is propagating. If the paint throws — plausible, since it repaints a document that a partially-applied `MemDocStore` batch left mid-edit — the paint error replaces the store error, losing the real cause.

samples.summary: Adoption adds a third whole-document `JSON.stringify` to every batch, i.e. to every keystroke
samples.evidence: `batch()` now computes `cloneDocument(this.doc)`, `JSON.stringify(beforeClone)`, and `JSON.stringify(top)` up front, plus `JSON.stringify(cloneDocument(this.doc))` at the end. Since `TextEditor.withUndoUnit()` now wraps every keystroke, each character typed in a MemDocStore host (docs demo, visual harness, slides text boxes) serialises the whole document four times instead of the previous three. Contained, but it scales with document size on the hottest path.

finding.summary: A transient share-link fetch failure now tears down the whole live editor session
finding.evidence: `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: 60_000`, `retry: 1` and the render guard `if (!token || error || !resolved)`. Two consecutive failed attempts ~1s apart — one offline blip, a 502, a laptop wake — unmount `SharedDocumentInner` and with it the Yorkie DocumentProvider/editor, replacing a working session with "Link unavailable" and discarding any local Yorkie changes not yet pushed. The comment claims only a "sustained failure" evicts, but nothing in the code distinguishes sustained from momentary (no `errorUpdateCount` threshold, no `resolved &&` fallback). verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: shared-document.tsx:1107-1119 defines the useQuery with refetchInterval SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS (60_000, line 88), staleTime 0, refetchOnWindowFocus true, retry 1, and line 1125 guards with `if (!token || error || !resolved)` before mounting SharedDocumentInner at line 1139. The project uses @tanstack/react-query ^5.74.4 (package.json:56), where a failed background refetch sets `error` while retaining previously fetched `data`; the guard short-circuits on `error` and therefore throws away a still-valid `resolved`. resolveShareLink (api/share-links.ts:99-111) throws via assertOk on any non-OK response (502/500/504) or rejected fetch, so transient server failures — not only revocation — trigger it; retry:1 only means two attempts ~1s apart and there is no errorUpdateCount threshold or `resolved &&` fallback, contrary to the comment's "sustained failure" claim. The app QueryClient has no defaultOptions (App.tsx:88) that would alter this, and SharedDocumentByToken is the only gate before SharedDocumentInner (line 1145-1148), so nothing elsewhere guards the path. Effect: the Yorkie DocumentProvider/editor subtree (SharedDocumentInner, line 926) unmounts and is replaced by "Link unavailable" (line 1132) on a momentary API blip. The only mitigating nuance (react-query default networkMode "online" pauses rather than errors when navigator.onLine is false) does not cover HTTP 5xx blips, so the defect remains reachable in normal use.

finding.summary: Undo floor now depends on reference identity of an SDK test-accessor's return value
finding.evidence: `canUndo()` was rewritten from a depth comparison to `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1`, where `stack` comes from `this.doc.getUndoStackForTest()`. This is only correct if that accessor returns the *live* internal array whose element identities are stable across calls. If the SDK returns a fresh/copied array of entries (or ever rebuilds an entry, e.g. during change transformation on remote merge), `lastIndexOf` yields -1 and `canUndo()` becomes unconditionally true — the initial-load floor disappears and a user can undo past `setDocument`, which the surrounding comment says 'would destroy blocks the cursor still references'. I could not verify the SDK behaviour: `node_modules` is not present in this checkout and only `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:58` describes the accessor ('arrays of reverse-op batches'). Worth confirming against @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.8 before relying on identity.

verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2997-3005 uses `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` over `doc.getUndoStackForTest()`, with the mark captured by reference at :885-888), but the asserted failure mode is contradicted by an in-repo counterexample. `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:344-357` asserts `store.canUndo() === false` immediately after `setDocument()` and again after undoing back to the floor; that can only pass if the accessor's top element is reference-identical to the captured mark. If the SDK rebuilt entries, `lastIndexOf` would be -1, `canUndo()` would be unconditionally true, and line 348 would fail. The test uses the real SDK (`import yorkie from '@yorkie-js/sdk'`, test file line 2), with no `vi.mock` and no alias/stub in `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:317-341` or `packages/frontend/tests/setup.ts`. The companion test at :365-386 pins the other branch (floor dropped by the 50-entry cap ⇒ all survivors undoable). Additionally, the finding's "fresh/copied array" half cannot break the code at all: a shallow copy preserves element identity; only entry rebuilding would, and that is precisely what these real-SDK tests rule out. The remaining "rebuild on remote merge" speculation is unverified by the reviewer and inconsistent with Yorkie's non-transforming undo stack, which the repo's own design notes (docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:400-412) rely on.

finding.summary: Making `resolved.role` live breaks the explicit "role is fixed for the route lifetime" assumption in slides-view and notes-view: an editor→viewer downgrade never reaches those editors
finding.evidence: This delta makes `resolved` (and hence `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, shared-document.tsx:383/460) change mid-session. docs-view and board-view list `readOnly` in their effect deps and rebuild, but slides-view.tsx:1222-1228 excludes `readOnlyMount` with the comment "it is derived from a share-link role that is fixed for the lifetime of the route, so toggling it at runtime is not a supported scenario", and notes-view.tsx:157 has deps `[didMount, doc]` with `readOnly` only consumed at `initialize(...)` (line 138). After a downgrade, a shared slides/notes session keeps a fully writable editor over a document whose link is now viewer-only — the exact hole this change sets out to close, left open for two of the five document types, and now on a path that actually fires.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claims are both contradicted by the working tree. (1) slides-view.tsx:1237 is `}, [didMount, doc, readOnlyMount]);` — `readOnlyMount` IS in the deps, and the comment at 1226-1235 explicitly states it is listed and load-bearing because "a share-link role is no longer fixed for the route's lifetime" (referencing SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS). The exclusion comment the reviewer quotes ("fixed for the lifetime of the route ... not a supported scenario") does not exist anywhere in packages/frontend/src (grep: no matches). (2) notes-view.tsx:167 is `}, [didMount, doc, readOnly]);` — not `[didMount, doc]` as claimed — with a comment at 156-165 stating the same rationale, so `initialize(...)` at line 138 is re-run and the editor/store rebuilt on an editor→viewer downgrade. `readOnlyMount` (slides-view.tsx:198) is derived from the `readOnly` prop and feeds initializeEditor (722), image paths (753), mountThumbnailPanel (1074) and mountNotesPanel (1077), all inside the effect that re-runs. The described hole is already closed for both cited document types.
